Write a letter or message to a worker serving on the field or far from home. Ask about body, soul, family and walk with God, not only about results. When writing to workers in restricted areas, avoid sensitive words.
Live out 235

Walk with your spiritual companions (2), be a spiritual parent and raise spiritual children (3), and join spiritual comrades in the fivefold ministry (5) as a team that prays and acts for one city or people group.
lessons.do: Today, choose one missionary from Pray for the Nations or your church’s mission prayer list. Write the missionary’s name in your Mission Journal, pray five minutes for him or her and the family, and then send a short message: “I prayed for you today. You are not alone.”
deep: How do I know whether I am called to go or called to send?

The Spirit’s call is usually not an isolated private feeling but something confirmed in community. Barnabas and Saul had already served faithfully in Antioch; the Spirit spoke while the church was serving together, and the leaders confirmed it with fasting, prayer and the laying on of hands. So serve faithfully where you are, stay open before the Lord in prayer, and ask your spiritual parents, pastors and team to discern with you. Neither going nor sending is second class; they are two hands of the same Great Commission.
Besides giving money, how else can I support missionaries?

Beyond finances, missionaries often need prayer, companionship and hospitality when they come home. You can pray regularly, learn about their field, remember their children’s names, pick them up at the airport and share a meal during home assignment, and listen patiently without rushing to ask about results. You can also lend your professional skills, such as translation, design or medical advice. For workers in sensitive regions, keep confidentiality: do not post their details, photos or whereabouts online.
lessons.quick: Some go and some send; goers lean on the Spirit, senders on prayer, all in one sending.
text: Now in the assembly that was at Antioch there were some prophets and teachers: Barnabas, Simeon who was called Niger, Lucius of Cyrene, Manaen the foster brother of Herod the tetrarch, and Saul.
As they served the Lord and fasted, the Holy Spirit said, “Separate Barnabas and Saul for me, for the work to which I have called them.”
Then, when they had fasted and prayed and laid their hands on them, they sent them away.
So, being sent out by the Holy Spirit, they went down to Seleucia. From there they sailed to Cyprus.
lessons.keyText: As they served the Lord and fasted, the Holy Spirit said, “Separate Barnabas and Saul for me, for the work to which I have called them.”

lessons.title: Every Nation and Tribe Before the Throne
lessons.sub: Mission ends in worship, as every people gives glory to the Lamb
lessons.hear:
When you work on a thousand-piece jigsaw puzzle, what you need most is the finished picture on the box lid; without it, a table full of pieces only discourages you. In its final book, the Bible shows us the picture on the lid: “After these things I looked, and behold, a great multitude which no man could count, out of every nation and of all tribes, peoples, and languages, standing before the throne and before the Lamb, dressed in white robes, with palm branches in their hands.” (Revelation 7:9)

This picture tells us three things. First, the goal of mission is worship. This crowd has not gathered to honor whichever missionary brought the most people to faith. They cry out with one voice, “Salvation be to our God, who sits on the throne, and to the Lamb!” (Revelation 7:10) Salvation belongs to God, not to those who preach; Jesus receives all the glory. Mission exists because worship is not yet complete. One day mission will end, but worship will go on forever and ever.

Second, God’s Kingdom is diverse and yet one. Every nation, tribe, people and language is there; the worship before the throne is not in one language or one culture. Taiwanese, Cantonese, Malay, Maori and sign language all praise the same Lamb. The gospel does not erase culture; it redeems it. It began with God’s promise to Abraham, “All the families of the earth will be blessed through you.” (Genesis 12:3), and it is fulfilled in Revelation. The whole Bible is one great mission story.

Third, the outcome is certain. No one can count that multitude, and God’s promise cannot fail. The Lamb has already “bought us for God with your blood out of every tribe, language, people, and nation” (Revelation 5:9). We are not fighting a battle whose outcome is in doubt; we are working under a King who has already won. Jesus said, “This Good News of the Kingdom will be preached in the whole world for a testimony to all the nations, and then the end will come.” (Matthew 24:14) Every testimony, every prayer for the nations and every missionary sent out moves us toward that day: toward the great end-time revival and the return of the Lord Jesus.

So walk backward from the throne into today. Since every people will be there on that day, pray for every people today. Since all the credit for salvation will go to God on that day, do not grab credit today. Since that crowd will be too great to count, we cannot be content with our own salvation; we must multiply disciples: “The things which you have heard from me among many witnesses, commit the same things to faithful men who will be able to teach others also.” (2 Timothy 2:2) Generation after generation, we build God’s system until “Let your Kingdom come” (Matthew 6:10) becomes reality before our eyes. On that day you will recognize names from your Gospel Friends List before the throne, and together you will say, “Amen!”
lessons.light: Self-centered mission revolves around me: counting how many I have reached and how large a ministry I have built, hoping for a place on heaven’s awards stage. Selfless mission revolves around the Lamb, knowing that salvation belongs to God and that I am just one in a multitude no one can count. Our focus is on the throne, not on ourselves. Mission begins in worship and is completed in worship.
think: Imagine yourself standing in the great multitude of Revelation 7. How does this picture change the way I see mission and other peoples and cultures?
In my ministry, do I secretly want a share of the credit for salvation? What are the signs?
For the sake of the day when the multitude is beyond counting, to whom can I pass on a disciple’s life now? Who is my next spiritual generation?
lessons.speak: God who sits on the throne, and the Lamb, blessing, glory, wisdom, thanksgiving, honor, power and might be to you forever and ever. Thank you for buying me with your blood out of every tribe and language, and for buying the nations too. Enlarge my heart to love every people you love. Deliver me from the self that craves credit, so that my whole life is lived for you to receive all the glory. Use me to make disciples and multiply disciples, building God’s system until your Kingdom comes. Come, Lord Jesus! In Jesus’ name, Amen.
prac: See the finish line
Copy out Revelation 7:9-10 and put it where you will see it often. Before you serve, remind yourself: the goal of mission is worship, and the glory belongs to the Lamb.
Pray for worship among every people
Each week, choose a country or people group in Pray for the Nations and ask God to let them worship him in their own language.
Taste the worship before the throne
Join a gathering in another language or culture, or learn a worship song in another language with your small group, and learn to appreciate the worship of other cultures.
Pass on what you have learned
Choose one person you can walk with, and following 2 Timothy 2:2, teach him or her the Six Steps of Gospel Conversation and how to share a testimony. Encourage that person to teach others as well.
Write your throne-room list
Beside your Gospel Friends List, write: “People I hope to see before the throne on that day.” Keep praying for them and keep taking steps of love toward them.
lessons.do: Today, quietly read Revelation 7:9-12 and picture that day. Speak the praise of Revelation 7:12 to God phrase by phrase. Then write in your Mission Journal the name of one person you are willing to begin walking with, someone who could one day teach others. Pray for that person and set a time to meet.
deep: If every nation and tribe stands before the throne, does that mean everyone will be saved in the end?

No. This multitude is “dressed in white robes,” and the passage explains that they have washed their robes and made them white in the blood of the Lamb (see Revelation 7:14). They are saved because they trust in the Lamb, not because they belong to a certain people. The picture tells us that some from every people will be saved, so the gospel must reach every people. It does not invite us to relax; it urges us to go, because people must hear and believe in order to be saved.
Isn’t talk of “welcoming the Lord’s return” too extreme, or even frightening?

Scripture forbids us to set dates, because no one knows that day or hour (see Matthew 24:36). Yet it also calls us to stay alert, be ready and work diligently, eagerly looking for the coming of the day of God (see 2 Peter 3:12). Welcoming the Lord’s return is not about stirring up fear or drawing up timetables; it is about living with an eternal perspective, investing our time, money and lives in what lasts forever: human souls and God’s Kingdom. The best way to prepare for his return is to do today’s work faithfully.
lessons.quick: Mission exists because worship is not yet complete; mission will end, but worship lasts forever.
text: After these things I looked, and behold, a great multitude which no man could count, out of every nation and of all tribes, peoples, and languages, standing before the throne and before the Lamb, dressed in white robes, with palm branches in their hands.
They cried with a loud voice, saying, “Salvation be to our God, who sits on the throne, and to the Lamb!”
All the angels were standing around the throne, the elders, and the four living creatures; and they fell on their faces before his throne, and worshiped God,
saying, “Amen! Blessing, glory, wisdom, thanksgiving, honor, power, and might, be to our God forever and ever! Amen.”
lessons.keyText: After these things I looked, and behold, a great multitude which no man could count, out of every nation and of all tribes, peoples, and languages, standing before the throne and before the Lamb, dressed in white robes, with palm branches in their hands.

verses.v: Go and make disciples of all nations, baptizing them in the name of the Father and of the Son and of the Holy Spirit, teaching them to observe all things that I commanded you. Behold, I am with you always, even to the end of the age.” Amen.
verses.p: Let Jesus reign first: all authority is in his hands. Going is obedience, not performance.

verses.v: Jesus therefore said to them again, “Peace be to you. As the Father has sent me, even so I send you.”
verses.p: As the Father sent Jesus into the world, Jesus sends you into your workplace and your home.

verses.v: But you will receive power when the Holy Spirit has come upon you. You will be witnesses to me in Jerusalem, in all Judea and Samaria, and to the uttermost parts of the earth.”
verses.p: It is not eloquence but the Spirit. Before you speak, ask: Holy Spirit, fill me and lead me.

verses.v: For I am not ashamed of the Good News of Christ, because it is the power of God for salvation for everyone who believes, for the Jew first, and also for the Greek.
verses.p: The gospel is not a sales pitch; it is the power of God. No need to be ashamed or anxious.

verses.v: We are therefore ambassadors on behalf of Christ, as though God were entreating by us: we beg you on behalf of Christ, be reconciled to God.
verses.p: You are Christ’s ambassador, not a salesperson. You plead; you don’t pressure.

verses.v: But sanctify the Lord God in your hearts. Always be ready to give an answer to everyone who asks you a reason concerning the hope that is in you, with humility and fear,
verses.p: First honor Christ as Lord in your heart, then be ready to answer. Gentleness matters more than winning.

verses.v: Walk in wisdom toward those who are outside, redeeming the time. Let your speech always be with grace, seasoned with salt, that you may know how you ought to answer each one.
verses.p: Let your words be gracious, seasoned with salt. Watch for the moment; you don’t have to say it all at once.

verses.v: Continue steadfastly in prayer, watching in it with thanksgiving, praying together for us also, that God may open to us a door for the word, to speak the mystery of Christ, for which I am also in bonds, that I may reveal it as I ought to speak.
verses.p: Ask God to open a door for the word, then ask to make the message clear.

verses.v: But when he saw the multitudes, he was moved with compassion for them because they were harassed and scattered, like sheep without a shepherd.
verses.p: See people as Jesus does: not their problems, but how harassed and scattered they are.

verses.v: Don’t you say, ‘There are yet four months until the harvest’? Behold, I tell you, lift up your eyes and look at the fields, that they are white for harvest already.
verses.p: Lift up your eyes: whose heart near you is already ready? Reach out to them today.

verses.v: For God didn’t give us a spirit of fear, but of power, love, and self-control. Therefore don’t be ashamed of the testimony of our Lord, nor of me his prisoner; but endure hardship for the Good News according to the power of God,
verses.p: Fear is not from God. Ask for power, love and self-control, and share in suffering for the gospel by his power.

verses.v: Haven’t I commanded you? Be strong and courageous. Don’t be afraid. Don’t be dismayed, for the LORD your God is with you wherever you go.”
verses.p: Wherever you go, God is with you. When afraid, read this aloud—then take one more step.

verses.v: But we have this treasure in clay vessels, that the exceeding greatness of the power may be of God and not from ourselves.
verses.p: You are a clay jar; the treasure is Christ. Your weakness shows the power is from God.

verses.v: They said, “Believe in the Lord Jesus Christ, and you will be saved, you and your household.”
verses.p: Pray for each family member by name. Let a changed life speak. Don’t force; don’t give up.

verses.v: My God will supply every need of yours according to his riches in glory in Christ Jesus.
verses.p: Sending and giving both rest on God’s supply. Entrust everything, and give thanks in everything.

verses.v: After these things I looked, and behold, a great multitude which no man could count, out of every nation and of all tribes, peoples, and languages, standing before the throne and before the Lamb, dressed in white robes, with palm branches in their hands. They cried with a loud voice, saying, “Salvation be to our God, who sits on the throne, and to the Lamb!”
verses.p: Lift your eyes to the finish line: every nation worshiping the Lamb. Today’s small step counts.

lp.v: Don’t you say, ‘There are yet four months until the harvest’? Behold, I tell you, lift up your eyes and look at the fields, that they are white for harvest already.
lp.p: Write this friend’s name, how you know them, what is happening in their life, and what they care about and need most.
lp.e: Ming, a coworker, 40. His father is in the hospital, he works late a lot, and he isn’t against faith but thinks it has nothing to do with him.

lp.v: who desires all people to be saved and come to full knowledge of the truth.
lp.p: God wants all people to be saved. Pray for them by name: ask God to open their heart and to open a door for you.
lp.e: Father, you want Ming to be saved. Comfort him as his father is ill, and give me a chance to care for him.

lp.v: Even so, let your light shine before men, that they may see your good works and glorify your Father who is in heaven.
lp.p: Which fruit of the Spirit do you want to show in front of them? Which self-centered habit needs to go first?
lp.e: I want to show patience and goodness: no complaining about the boss behind his back, and helping carry his load when we work late.

lp.v: To the weak I became as weak, that I might gain the weak. I have become all things to all men, that I may by all means save some.
lp.p: Plan one or two things you can do with them. Enter their world. People matter more than tasks—they are not a project.
lp.e: Lunch with him this week to ask about his father; next week bring a small snack to the hospital.

lp.v: But sanctify the Lord God in your hearts. Always be ready to give an answer to everyone who asks you a reason concerning the hope that is in you, with humility and fear,
lp.p: Prepare a two-to-three-minute salvation story or one fitting verse, and wait for the Spirit’s moment to share it gently.
lp.e: When he says “I’m exhausted,” share how I met Jesus in my lowest season, and Matthew 11:28.

lp.v: Nathanael said to him, “Can any good thing come out of Nazareth?” Philip said to him, “Come and see.”
lp.p: What could you invite them to—small group, a gospel dinner, reading a Gospel together? When will you follow up?
lp.e: Invite him to next month’s gospel dinner; if he is open, read a passage of John with him each week.

five.v: that you were at that time separate from Christ, alienated from the commonwealth of Israel, and strangers from the covenants of the promise, having no hope and without God in the world.
five.p: In a sentence or two: what were you chasing, fearing, or missing inside? Be honest without exaggerating.
five.e: I worked nonstop to prove my worth. I looked fine outside, but inside I was often empty and anxious.

five.v: He therefore answered, “I don’t know if he is a sinner. One thing I do know: that though I was blind, now I see.”
five.p: How did God find you—a person, a word, a verse, an event? Keep the spotlight on Jesus, not yourself.
five.e: A coworker prayed for me at my lowest point, and I heard for the first time, “Come to me, all you who labor and are heavily burdened.”

five.v: Therefore if anyone is in Christ, he is a new creation. The old things have passed away. Behold, all things have become new.
five.p: Name one or two concrete changes—in thinking, emotions, or family. Don’t pretend life has no troubles now.
five.e: I still get tired, but I no longer have to prove my worth. I’ve learned to apologize to my family, and I sleep in peace.

five.t: What the Lord has done for me
five.v: He didn’t allow him, but said to him, “Go to your house, to your friends, and tell them what great things the Lord has done for you and how he had mercy on you.”
five.p: Choose a verse that carried you through, and say what it means to you.
five.e: “Peace I leave with you” carried me through the year my father died.

five.v: “Come, see a man who told me everything that I have done. Can this be the Christ?”
five.p: End with one pressure-free sentence inviting them to come and meet Jesus too.
five.e: If you’d like, I’d love to read the Gospel of John with you and see who Jesus is.

min.v: praying together for us also, that God may open to us a door for the word, to speak the mystery of Christ, for which I am also in bonds,
min.d: Pray for them by name. Ask God to open a door, and ask the Spirit to guard your heart and words. Recall their situation; prepare one verse and your salvation story.
min.s: (Silently) Lord, I’m not going to win an argument. Love them through me, and let them meet you.

min.v: So, then, my beloved brothers, let every man be swift to hear, slow to speak, and slow to anger;
min.d: Start with their life: work, family, stress and hopes. Ask more, say less, listen well, and reflect back now and then.
min.s: “How’s work lately?” “Which part of that pressure wears you out most?”

min.v: Paul stood in the middle of the Areopagus and said, “You men of Athens, I perceive that you are very religious in all things. For as I passed along and observed the objects of your worship, I also found an altar with this inscription: ‘TO AN UNKNOWN GOD.’ What therefore you worship in ignorance, I announce to you.
min.d: Find a bridge from their needs, questions or values: peace, meaning, forgiveness, death, family. Respect their views; don’t rush to rebut.
min.s: “You said you want real peace. I’ve longed for that too. May I share what happened to me?”

min.v: For I delivered to you first of all that which I also received: that Christ died for our sins according to the Scriptures, that he was buried, that he was raised on the third day according to the Scriptures,
min.d: With permission, say it simply: God loves us; sin separates us from God; Christ died for us and rose again; receive him by faith. Add your story.
min.s: “The Bible says Christ died for our sins according to the Scriptures, and was raised on the third day…”

min.v: Behold, I stand at the door and knock. If anyone hears my voice and opens the door, then I will come in to him and will dine with him, and he with me.
min.d: Gently ask what they think and invite a response—no pressure. If they are ready, lead a simple prayer of faith; if not, respect that and invite them to keep exploring.
min.s: “Jesus is knocking at the door of your heart. Would you like to open the door to him now, or get to know him more first?”

min.v: I planted. Apollos watered. But God gave the increase.
min.d: Afterward, note their response and what you promised, and check in within three days. Connect new believers quickly with a church and small group to read the Bible and prepare for baptism.
min.s: “I’ll be praying for you this week. Shall we read the Gospel of John together next week?”

rules: Be with God first
Mission is not busy activity; it flows from our relationship with God. Be won by Christ, then win others for him.
Keep the focus on Jesus
We proclaim Jesus, not our church, our culture or ourselves. Results and glory belong to the Lord.
People over tasks
People are never numbers or results. Never harm a relationship for the sake of decisions.
Listen before speaking
Respect their story and views; ask more, say less. Don’t win arguments—win hearts.
No pressure, no manipulation
Never use fear, guilt, gain or emotion to push a decision. Faith is the Spirit’s work.
Respect culture and law
Distinguish the gospel from your own culture; obey local laws and customs; in restricted areas follow your agency and local church.
Team and covering
Don’t go it alone: have a sending church, spiritual covering and partners; pray through major decisions with your agency and pastor.
Safety and boundaries
Meet the opposite sex in public or with a partner; involve parents when minors are involved; never post identities, photos or locations of missionaries or local believers.
Financial integrity
Keep gifts and funds transparent and used as designated; never trade money or goods for decisions.
Disciple to the end
A decision is only the beginning. Bring new believers into church community, walk with them as disciples, and send them to make disciples.

s: Check in
Ask about their week; listen to their feelings and struggles.
Read a Gospel together
Read a short Gospel passage (John is a great start); each shares the line that stood out.
See Jesus
Ask: what does this show you about who Jesus is? What did he do for people?
Connect to life
Ask: if this is true, what difference does it make for you? How would you respond?
Pray and bless
With permission, pray briefly for them and set the next time to read together.
Praise the Lord of the nations
Praise God with a song or two and a passage. Let God be God.
Mission update
Share news of one country, people group or missionary—brief and specific.
Pray for the nations
In small groups, pray by name for that nation, people, local church and missionaries.
Pray for gospel friends
Each names one or two gospel friends; pray for each other and ask God to open doors.
Listen and send
Listen quietly to the Spirit: who will go, who will send? Pray the Lord’s Prayer and bless one another.
Meal and welcome
Share a meal or tea; warmly welcome first-time guests so they feel accepted.
Icebreaker
Ask an everyday question everyone can answer, such as “What made you happiest lately?”
Life question
Use a short video, story or life question (stress, meaning, family, forgiveness) to open the topic.
Story and message
One member shares a salvation story; then use a Gospel passage to explain briefly who Jesus is.
Discussion
Talk freely in groups of three to five. Respect every view—no arguing, no pressure.
Prayer and invitation
Pray for those who are willing; gently invite anyone curious to a one-on-one reading or the next gathering.

timer.p: Set everything aside, come before the Lord, and let Christ’s love take hold of you first.

timer.t: Praise the Lord of the nations
timer.p: Let God be God: praise him as King of the nations; may his name be great among the peoples.

timer.t: Confess and return to your place
timer.p: Let people be people: confess coldness, fear, or living only in your own small world.

timer.t: Pray for gospel friends by name
timer.p: Open your Gospel Friends List and pray for each one’s salvation by name.
Pray for one country, one people group, the local church and missionaries. Ask the Lord of the harvest to send workers.
Listen quietly: to whom is the Spirit sending you this week? Are you to go, or to send?
Entrust your friends and the nations to the Lord. Yours is the kingdom, the power and the glory.
